Things aren't absolute. Yes, in absolute terms Israel has a lot of issues, but I'm saying you compare Israel to other places, and it seems right now that Israel will probably emerge as a dominant power in the Middle East after this war in Iran is done with.

## AI competition and the limits of prediction

### Who benefits from portraying China as America's main rival?

Audience: So many media portray China as the U.S.'s main rival. Who benefits from the narrative, and why?

Response: It's really the Americans who benefit from the narrative that China is the main rival, specifically U.S. tech companies. You're Sam Altman or you're an AI company, and everyone's asking you, why are we investing so much in data centers when we're not actually deriving much value from your AI services? If I had a choice whether to have water and electricity for free or ChatGPT for free, I'm always going to pick water and electricity, because I need water and electricity to survive and to live a good life, whereas I don't actually need ChatGPT.

The only response these companies have is, well, if we don't do it, then China will do it. Do you want China to get AGI first? Because China will get AGI first if we don't actually invest in data centers. Meanwhile, I think the United States has ten times as many data centers as China, so it's absurd.

The function of the media is to cause fear and anxiety in the United States, because fear and anxiety cause obedience. They're always coming up with these narratives to scare people. Right now, honestly, they're focusing a lot on the China narrative. But honestly, no one's scared of China because, back in the Cold War, yeah, Russia was scary. Russians are not afraid to die, and Russia will kick your ass in a fight. China, Chinese people, no, no. You've gone to school with Chinese kids. You know what they're like. They are not a threat.

### What if AGI arrives within the next few years?

Audience: I know you believe that AGI is not something that will come about within the next couple of years. But if you're wrong in that regard, how do you think that will affect the U.S.–China relationship moving forward once that is created?

Response: Let's game-theory this out. Let's just say, for example, they're able to achieve AGI. Whichever nation is able to achieve AGI first will obviously dominate. But here's my question. I'm just using game theory. Why would other nations be hostile towards this AGI?

The United States achieves AGI, and China's like, does that mean we shut our borders and not allow our people to access this AGI? Or do we allow our people to access this AGI because we know that it will bring much more economic benefits to us? If I am a politician in China, do I care who actually controls this AGI? All I care about is staying in power more.

The example I use, there is an analogy, which is the U.S. dollar. The United States controls the world's currency, and that's an absurd power. It's almost as powerful, even more powerful than the idea of AGI. China could have been like, screw this, we're not going to trade with the U.S. dollar because that would destroy our national sovereignty, which would be a legitimate argument. But what happened? China did trade in the U.S. dollar, and China became very wealthy because of its trade with the U.S. dollar. Its people became much more productive. They were able to build better infrastructure. People were able to travel around the world and learn more knowledge.

My question then is, if the United States were the first to achieve AGI, why would China actually be hostile towards this AGI? Why would China be like, no, we have to create our own AGI? They wouldn't care. They'd be like, if AGI means our economy becomes stronger, if AGI means that our political system becomes much stronger, then we will adopt it. I think this would be true for every country.

Now, let's just say China were to be the first to achieve AGI. This would be a problem for the United States because the United States would not surrender its sovereignty over to this Chinese AGI. It would benefit China to achieve this AGI, and honestly, this is why, if you look at Chinese policy these past five years, China has gone all in on AGI.

But again, I'm not really sure if China were to achieve AGI, if that would be a good thing for China, because the United States still controls the U.S. dollar. The United States could, in theory, choose to embargo China. China has this AGI, but Japan, India, Southeast Asia, Australia have chosen to embargo China. How would the AGI respond to that? It couldn't respond to that, because nuclear weapons. Then how about Russia? Would Russia surrender its sovereignty to this Chinese AGI? Probably not.

It's a really absurd situation where if America were to achieve AGI first, then the world would basically follow the American lead, especially China. But if China were to achieve AGI first, then the United States would basically declare war on China.

### Are the rumors about Xi's health different this time?

Audience: Regarding the analysis about Xi looking a little frail, a little unhealthy, ever since he came to power in 2012, it's like a seasonal thing where if he disappears for a week or two, people start talking about, did something happen? He always reappears. There's been so many false alarms. I personally have an attitude of whenever something happens to him, it's going to happen, but you can't read the tea leaves or anticipate it because he always comes back, every time so far.

What makes these recent signals he's giving, or observations that people are making—is there anything different about them, or is this just another false alarm, so to speak? Also, regarding something you said in your Substack about Chinese whispers , you said that there's a rumor about Bo Xilai potentially being freed from prison and somehow staging some political action. Bo himself is already 77 years old. How would that rumor have any wings when somebody's been in prison since 2012 and is already 77 years old? How would something like that possibly work?

Response: You make a great point, which is throughout the years there's always been rumors about Xi's health. The most serious rumor is he actually suffered a stroke a couple years ago, and this explains the paralysis in the Chinese system. I did say throughout this presentation that through a series of events, he was able to consolidate power and install his friends, his cronies, his associates into very important positions of power, especially in the military. But over time they've been purged.

The question then is, how did he lose so much power? The answer is, apparently, the rumor is—again, this is all rumors; we have absolutely no idea—during a very important meeting, he had a stroke, and he was hospitalized for a few days. While he was away, that allowed different political factions to get together and go after all his associates, and that's why we have this paralysis right now in the Chinese system. Again, this is only a rumor. I have absolutely no idea if this is true. If it were true, it would actually help us explain a lot.

My main question, my main problem with what's going on in China right now is a sense of deep paralysis. Again, I live and work in China. It doesn't feel as though someone is in control. All the reporting about Xi is that he's a very authoritarian person. He's very strong-willed. He's very domineering. But in China, again, it doesn't feel as though the country is moving towards a certain direction.

Let's just game-theory this. If someone were in charge, what would be happening? First of all, I think what would be happening is basically the beginnings of preparation for war against Taiwan, to reclaim Taiwan. You would see that in the Chinese media. You would see that in schools. You would basically see a rally around the flag. That's number one.

Number two is you would see the emergence of some national champions that are heavily supported by the state. You do have some of these AI companies, but it seems very much like a lot of these companies are not as energetic as you would think they are.

Number three is you would see a much stronger Chinese voice on the geopolitical stage. Remember, back ten years ago, there was this huge trend of wolf-warrior diplomacy, where you had these very outspoken Chinese diplomats speaking the Chinese narrative in different places. They were very aggressive, but it was clear they were being supported by a very strong central authority. Nowadays, you don't have these people. You don't have any real spokesperson for the Chinese interest on the geopolitical stage.

It's very weird how you have this war in Ukraine, you have this war in Iran, and there's no real spokesperson representing the Chinese interest. You have someone like Professor Morandi representing the Iranian interest, but you don't have a designated figure going on Piers Morgan or CNN or BBC, just speaking out the Chinese interest. That, to me, is really weird, and that suggests they don't really have a narrative they want to present.

All of this is really weird to me, and my only explanation is the country is in paralysis. Why is the country in paralysis? There's no leader in charge. But again, I could be wrong. I do see some stark contrast between Xi's first five years in office and these past two years, especially in terms of wolf-warrior diplomacy, especially in terms of presenting an international agenda.

Remember, in his first five-year term, he emphasized the Chinese Dream a lot, the idea of an emergent China on the world stage. Now he doesn't even talk about the Chinese Dream anymore. That is his singular idea, and he doesn't really talk about it. In fact, he doesn't talk about any ideas, and that's weird, because traditionally these Chinese leaders do have a slogan or a theme that captures the essence of what they're trying to achieve. I don't know what he's trying to achieve. Maybe Taiwanese reunification, but that's not really discussed anymore in China, which is really weird.

### Could powerful leaders extend their lifespans?

Audience: I also remember that last year, at the commemoration for World War II, Putin and Xi were caught talking on the hot mic about possibly extending lifespan with new technologies. Is that just idle talk, or is that a real possibility for people with that kind of power to live at a functioning, healthy age long term that normal people don't have access to? I know that in a recent talk in the U.S., you said there's no guarantee that the leaders would die at any normal timeline.

Response: Look at Putin, who is, again, in his seventies, and he looks extremely alert. He looks pretty healthy. Modi is also someone who looks pretty alert, pretty healthy. I do think they have access to the best technology.

Let's just assume that there is this factional struggle within China right now. Actually, it would be in the best interest of President Xi to look sick and unwell in order to throw his opponents off. Remember, it's not hard for these guys to get together and overthrow him. But the problem is, what happens afterwards? They don't actually trust each other. They're always scrambling to figure out. They're opportunistic. They're speculative. They're trying to position themselves into power. In China, the general rule is whoever is the first to act is the first to die.

### What happens to nuclear weapons during a collapse?

Audience: With the coming Bronze Age-like collapse and civil wars, what would happen to countries which have nuclear weapons, like China, which I recently read was increasing its nuclear arsenal?

Response: Basically, if there's a Bronze Age collapse, then a lot of the struggle is domestic and internal, which basically means you just can't use these nuclear weapons. Over time, what happens is the state's capacity to deploy these nuclear weapons becomes degraded. You need a lot of upkeep and maintenance to maintain these nuclear weapons. If you don't have the resources, then they get ignored, and then they're just not used.

### Did Fulton Sheen's beatification overshadow Xi's visit?

Audience: One thing that hasn't been mentioned, and I don't know if you saw this, but I find it really intriguing: the beatification of Archbishop Fulton Sheen happened yesterday, which is the same day Trump hosted Xi for the state dinner and everything at the White House. What I find so ironic is Fulton Sheen was an incredibly popular American advocate against communism.

A super, super famous story in the 1950s: it was actually the story of a ten-year-old Chinese girl named Little Li, who was martyred in China during the Communist Revolution, that inspired his big devotion to a daily holy hour. I don't know if you know that story, but I find it so odd that this date of Fulton Sheen's beatification, which 50,000 people filled a football stadium for in St. Louis, and it had all this media coverage, it really overshadowed Xi's visit.

This date for Fulton Sheen's beatification was picked six months ago by the Vatican, which is probably before China and the U.S. made their arrangement. Do you think that is just pure coincidence, or do you think it was maybe an insult to Xi, especially since Trump was complaining that the media didn't cover his event, because there's all the White House media ban, all that drama going on? But meanwhile, all these grassroots news agencies were covering this feel-good, happy, grassroots, we love America, we are so not communist.

I wanted to know if you saw the alignment of those two events, and how Fulton Sheen was inspired by the martyrdom of a ten-year-old Chinese girl. I want to know your thoughts on perhaps the religious vein in all of this.

Response: I actually have absolutely no idea about who he is and his relationship to China. I think it's a coincidence. It's very hard for me to imagine they actually planned this out and picked a date when President Xi would be in the United States, because remember something really important: they only confirmed that President Xi would visit the United States two days prior to his actual visit. There was actually a health scare where he was in India, and he skipped the state dinner, and he had to go back to China. I don't know how much planning goes into these things.

What I will say, though, is I think people are just underwhelmed by this visit. I had some expectations that there would be some surprises, and it's been very underwhelming. It almost seems like a rehash of the May visit, but not as interesting. I think there's just not that much media coverage of the visit, and there's been very little commentary. I don't think people are that interested in the China visit. That's what I find really interesting, how there just doesn't seem that much interest out there.

Audience: If you don't know who Fulton Sheen is, look him up on YouTube sometime. He was a very entertaining TV star back in his day.

## The dollar, AI policy, and the speaker's outlook

### How long can the U.S. dollar hold on?

Audience: You talked about the U.S. dollar crashing and coming to an end. But before it's going to come to an end, you said after the Chinese visit, it's going to probably return back to normal levels somehow. We've already seen it reviving. Do you see this happening for the next one, two years, or for a couple of months until the war returns? How do you see the dollar hanging around?

Response: I think it's very hard to replace the U.S. dollar. I think in the worst-case scenario there'll be other currencies that challenge the dominance of the U.S. dollar, and it's possible you will have these different trading blocs emerge. But honestly, and this is not financial advice, honestly, if I had wealth, I would just keep it in U.S. Treasuries, the most liquid.

I'm not saying this because I think U.S. Treasuries are the best investment. There are probably some other investments that give a better return on investment. I'm just saying U.S. Treasuries are just the most convenient. You can do the most with U.S. Treasuries. I think that in a time of uncertainty, you want the most flexibility.

### How do you see the ICE situation in the United States?

Audience: At the moment, I'm living in the U.S. as an immigrant. I've been here for four years. My question is, how do you see the ICE situation all around the U.S.? Do you think it's safe for me? I've seen locally ICE is around, so I'm always careful where I'm going. I try to stay at home most of the time. I go to work, but I'm just afraid that they will close the borders and I end up trapped. I'm originally from Mexico. What do you think?

Response: It's hard for me to comment on this because I'm not American. It's really hard for me to make a judgment. I think ICE's power will only grow, but I think it's possible ICE shifts its focus from dealing with illegal immigrants to dealing with cities that don't cooperate. I think ICE is slowly becoming a police force, a personal police force for Donald Trump. But it's very hard for me to comment.

### Could Xi help Trump obtain a third term or a Nobel Peace Prize?

Audience: Do you think Xi is supporting Trump to get his third term by mediating between Iran and the U.S. to make a good Nobel Peace Prize theater?

Response: I think this is much too clever. I think Trump doesn't need Xi and Putin's help to get a third term. But what I do think is that the three—Trump, Xi, and Putin—do benefit from global chaos in order to degrade the power of the globalists, especially the Europeans and the Canadians, the City of London, basically.

I think that at some point the three will get together and propose maybe a new world order where the three countries, and possibly Iran, get together and agree on a new global order of stability, and that will get Trump the Nobel Peace Prize. I think that's what might happen.

### Will regulation restrict open-source AI?

Audience: Currently, the U.S. AI companies, I assume they're trying to pressure Trump into releasing new AI regulations in order to prevent competition so they can monopolize it themselves. But they're also in a situation where they're treating Chinese AI companies as the main threat. We have to make sure we outcompete these guys. Will the U.S. eventually try to release regulations that prevent open-source AI models from being run by smaller companies or individuals, and then just only allow the big companies like Claude or OpenAI or whatever?

Response: I don't know enough about the industry to comment, but I will make two guesses. Guess number one is they will definitely block Chinese open-source models from entering the United States. That's pretty obvious. My prediction number two is they're actually much more interested in securing government funding for their projects. What that might mean is a nationalization of data centers, where the government assumes the cost of running these data centers, and then these AI companies can just run their models. I don't know enough about the industry, but those are my two guesses.

Audience: Right now, the big thing used to compare the different models is benchmarks. If Chinese open-source AIs get cut off from the United States, how would people compare the performances between the two and say, oh, the Chinese are still right on the U.S.'s tail, so we need to keep doing more funding?

Response: I don't think they care. I think you're right. I think all they're interested in is creating a monopoly, and that means controlling the levers of policy in Washington, D.C.

### Is U.S.–China AI competition theater?

Audience: I just share from the AI industry. All the investors in China AI, like Hillhouse Capital, like the co-founder of the Alibaba Group, all the guys graduated from the same university as yours, from Yale. The AI competition between the U.S. and China is theater. In fact, the investor in China AI robotics is the U.S. venture capital fund. They are transnational agents. They graduated from the same university, Yale University.

Also, Professor, I find a reason why you were admitted by Yale, because they have the guy named Henry Luce. He's the founder of Time magazine, Fortune magazine. Every single U.S. reader is educated and funded by this guy. This guy is the founder of the American Century. This guy was born in the seventies. Since it's theater, the competition between the USA and China, what will happen?

Response: As you point out, I think you're right. I think a lot of this is theater. I think what's going to happen is an AI takeover of government in both places.

### How does a BRICS gold-backed system compare with the petrodollar?

Audience: I'm wondering about the BRICS gold-backed system that China launched out of Hong Kong. What's your take on that and the petrodollar?

Response: The difference between the petrodollar and the BRICS system is, in the petrodollar, you have a hegemon. What a hegemon is, is a dispute-resolution mechanism, like a godfather. You don't have that in BRICS. What's been happening is no one can actually agree on anything. Unless China's willing to employ or deploy military force to resolve conflicts, then no one's going to take China seriously.

The idea that we all sit together and we all get along never works. If you actually have people coming together and sitting around and trying to come to a decision, it will never, ever work. You always need someone in charge, and unfortunately China is not willing to do this. For China to be in charge, it either needs to deploy its military, which it doesn't want to do, or it needs to be the global reserve currency. But the global reserve currency just means you have open capital markets, and China doesn't want to do that either.

It's a ridiculous situation where China doesn't want to assume any of the risks and liabilities, but it wants everyone to get along, which never happens.

### Are Chinese elites studying Kabbalah?

Audience: Do you think there are some Chinese elites who are trying to study Kabbalah?

Response: The answer is they're not because it's too hard. Kabbalah is a very complex tradition. It's pretty simple if you're Jewish, because you need to both access the Bible as well as the occult. The Chinese elite, my God, they're not that bright, and they're kind of lazy too.

### Has traveling changed your view of China and the United States?

Audience: You touched on this briefly, I think, in your Los Angeles talk, where you were always confused about your American friends coming to China and being enamored with everything. Then when you stepped into L.A., you felt like you understood their perspective much more. Now that you've had a little time away from the States, can you speak on how your perspective might have shifted, whether you look at China differently or whether you look at the U.S. differently after not being there for several years?

Response: You're absolutely right in that when I was in China for too long, I tended to maybe judge China too harshly, and I tended to perceive the U.S. in a more positive light. That's just human nature. After spending a month in the United States, how do I feel about the U.S.? How do I feel about China?

I don't think the United States is heading in the right direction. I don't think China is heading in the right direction. My desire is to explore more of the world so I can get a more global perspective. But I am not optimistic about either the United States or China. I think both countries have a lot of issues. I think these issues will become much more clear in a year or two.

I will also say that regardless of the issues in the United States, the United States is still a nicer place to live than China. One main takeaway I've had these two months of traveling North America is I really don't want to go back to China, man. I really hate China. I don't like people spitting on the streets everywhere. I don't like people bumping each other, pushing each other around. I don't like people just cursing each other out for the most minor things. I don't like the pollution in China.

I'm spending some time in the woods in Canada. I love the fact that my kid can just explore the woods by himself with his friends. I think that's how kids should just grow up, and you can't do that in China. I'm looking to get out of China as soon as possible. But I do understand the limitations and problems in North America as well.

### How do you respond to concerns that your predictions create anxiety?

Audience: I have a very transparent and open question. My cousin and I have been listening to you for a while now, and the things you talk about are really enlightening. You go very deep on a lot of things that I think are not said. One criticism of you that constantly comes up with me and my cousins when we talk about these things is, I feel like a lot of podcasters and people in general nowadays say things that stir up a lot of anxiety in people. Obviously, times are bad, and it causes people to worry about the future.

One criticism that's come up of you a lot is that you have some sort of ulterior motive, whether people are saying that because you're from China, that might have something to do with it, where you're trying to stir up something, or whatever it is, some ulterior motive. My cousin and me, we're on the side of no. We truly believe you're doing it because you want to better the world. You have a mission, you want to just expose truth, basically. We always defend you, but what would you say to that if that question came up to you?

Response: It's a great question, and something I struggle with every day. My main response is very simple: I try to make predictions. But the reason why I try to make predictions is I think that we as humans have the capacity to control our own fate through our own analysis. What I'm trying to do is teach people how to think for themselves. To validate my model, I make predictions. How do you know if my analysis is correct? If my predictions turn out to be correct.

I blew up because of the Iran war. If you go back two years, when I was making these predictions, everyone online would call me crazy for saying that the United States would attack Iran, because they'd be like, why would we do that? That's insane. But it happened, and that's why I blew up online. Just because I became popular online doesn't mean I'm going to sit back and just make money. My mission is to educate people.

Now I'm making new predictions, but it's all based on my game-theory model of the world. That's what I'm trying to do. I'm trying to teach people. You don't have to listen to what I say. If you listen to what I say, what I hope you're doing is listening carefully as to how I'm making my analysis. That's actually more important than my predictions.

What you also find is I'm willing to admit when I'm wrong, and then go back and analyze my model and figure out where I went wrong. That's my main response.

# Global Meet-Up #6 (Montreal): The Supremacy of Sin

## The nature of evil and sin

Today's lecture is on Sabbatean-Frankism: the nature of evil and sin in this world. And today's lecture is going to be different from other lectures I've done in the past because today's lecture I'm going to ask you guys to use your imagination a lot. We're going to try to get into the minds of the people who run this world to understand the psychology and to better understand why they do what they do—their behavior.

## Superpowers and anxiety

We’re going to start with a thought experiment. Let's just say you're back in high school and you go on a science field trip to a laboratory and you're with your classmates and then for some reason a radioactive spider escapes from the lab and bites you. You feel kind of sick. So you ask to go home and you sleep it off. The next morning you get up and you feel very different. You feel stronger. You feel lighter. You feel faster when you jump. You can jump up to the ceiling.

In fact, you find that you have a desire to touch the wall and climb the wall. And so you climb up the building. When you run, you run really fast. You find that it's easy for you to lift things like a car. You just lift the car. You have super strength, you have super vision, you can climb. At first you're excited, and maybe you join the basketball team and you become a star player. But after a while, after a few months, this excitement actually becomes anxiety.

Because you are special, but you don't know why you're special. Why is it that there are 8 billion people in this world, but you're different from everyone else? And you can logically explain it. You can be like, "Well, I was on a field trip and I got bitten by a radioactive spider and so that’s what happened." But the explanation is not complete. You have to believe that it was not just a radioactive spider. Maybe it was a spiritual force, God or a demon. You don't know. But something powerful chose you and it causes anxiety in you. You want to know what's really going on. You want to know what the truth of the universe is. And we call this the occult.

So when you have a special power, yes, for the first few months, for the first few years, you enjoy it. But eventually this excitement leads to anxiety. You can't sleep. You can't help but feel fear and anxiety. You want to know what the truth of the universe is. You want to know who gave you this power and why this person gave you this power. So you study the occult. You want to ask yourself, are you the Messiah?

Is this a messianic mission? Were you given this special power by God or Satan in order to accomplish a special mission on this world? You cannot help but feel this. I know. And again, I know this feels strange, but I guarantee you if you were bitten by radioactive spider and you have all these special powers, eventually you're going to ask this question. Why did God pick me? That's the first thing. The first thing is you feel anxiety. You want to know who picked you and what your mission is.

But then what happens next is you feel really lonely. And the loneliness and alienation is another source of anxiety. You want to know: "I’m special, but are there other special people in this world?" And how do I find them? And how do I work with them? Because what I really want to do is keep my power. What you find is, "I enjoy this power." How do I keep this power? How do I preserve this power? How do I extend this power?

Because the great fear of course is the government will come and imprison you to experiment on you, right? You have this fear, you have this anxiety. And so the best way to preserve yourself is to find other people like yourself and work together in order to amass more power, in order to preserve your power, in order to enjoy your life. And this is why we have secret societies. Because if you are in a position of power, you feel anxiety and there are three sources of this anxiety. First of all, you don't know why or where you got this power from.

You have to explain it. That's why you're studying the occult. Second is you have a deep desire to preserve, to protect your power from others. And the only way to do that is to find others like you and to work together. Otherwise the government could come and just kidnap you and experiment on you. And the third thing of course is now that you have the special power, you want more of it. And this psychology helps us understand the psychology of the elite. People like Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin, Peter Thiel, anyone with more power, with more fame, with more wealth than anyone else. They all think like this.

And what is it that allows them to amass so much power, wealth, and fame? What is your superpower?

## Sin as a superpower

So if you look at the elite, what their superpower is is sin . In other words, the people in charge, the people with all the power, money, and wealth in the world, it is not because they are smarter than we are. It is not because they are more hardworking than we are. It's because they are more amoral than we are. So to understand this, let's do another thought experiment. And the thought experiment is very easy. You are put into a room.

You stand in the room. Sitting across from you is a man in a hood. A black hood. You can't see the man. You don't know the man. And there's a table separating you two. And on the table is a handgun. Someone comes into the room and says to you, "If you take the gun and shoot to death the man in the hood, I'll give you $10,000."

And you think about it: "That’s not a lot of money. $10,000 to kill someone. I’m not gonna do it." So, you say no. Then the authority says to you, "I’ll give you a million dollars." You’re like, "Wow, a million dollars is really good. I can buy maybe half a house in Montreal now, right?" But you're like, "Yeah, but that's still not enough." And then the guy is like, "I'll give you $10 million."

And you're like, "$10 million is now life-changing." And, "Yeah, I’ll do it." So you agree to do it. But then what happens is this. You try to pick up the gun, but your hand shakes. You can't pick it up. You're paralyzed. You've agreed to do it. You want to do it. You want the money, but you're paralyzed. You can't do it. That's most of us. That is 99.9999% of us. At a certain amount of money, $10 million, $100 million, a billion dollars, who knows, we will agree to kill the other person in the hood. But when we try to do it, we can't do it.

We're paralyzed. We're frozen by we don't know what. Maybe our morality, maybe our conscience, maybe an angel protecting us. Who knows? What separates the elite, what makes people like Jeff Bezos, Peter Thiel, Sam Altman unique is they can do this. They can take the gun, point at the person, shoot it, and not feel anything afterwards. That is what separates the elite from everyone else. They are killers. So it is their capacity to sin that is a superpower.

And because they have the capacity to sin, this separates them from everyone else. This allows them to accumulate more power than anyone else. But then this creates the anxiety in them, right? Why do I have the superpower to sin? Who gave it to me? How do I find other people like myself so that we can work together to amass more power?

### Is the superpower the capacity to wash away sin?

Audience question:

I imagine the next Sam Altman or the next Peter Thiel is somewhere out there, right? And he could be anybody, right? I feel like at some point they would have felt that same conscience when they had to make that decision, a critical decision that had a level of morality to it. I feel like they would still feel it, but it's more the superpower is the capacity to wash that sin.

Professor Jiang:

Yeah. Things will become a lot clearer once I finish the lecture. The capacity to sin is a great superpower in the world we have today. ## The Glorious Revolution and the Bank of England

1688 was a very crucial year. 1688 was something called the Glorious Revolution. And the Glorious Revolution was an agreement between the English nobility and the Dutch nobility to merge together. And the way they did that was they transferred the wealth of the Dutch Republic, all the gold, to England. And then in 1694 this arrangement became corporatized, systemized. 1694 was the year that the Bank of England was chartered.

What is the Bank of England and why is it special? Before, in European history, kings, in order to finance wars, would borrow money from merchants, right? And merchants would lend the money to kings in order to grow their capital. The problem with that is the king could die, the king could lose the war, or the king could just be like, "I will not honor this contract." So this created a lot of risk for merchants. The Bank of England solved this problem by creating a situation where the private owners of the Bank of England were the merchants. And the organization that borrowed money from the Bank of England was not the king. It was the people of England. Through Parliament.

Remember, before, the king had the power to issue currency. Now the merchants have the power to issue currency, but it is backed by Parliament which is the people. And to make this system palatable to everyone, new ideas were created in order to justify the system. The first major idea that was created was private property. The sanctity of private property. # Global Meet-Up #7 (Toronto): The Rupture

## The rupture

This is a term that Mark Carney used earlier this year at the World Economic Forum to describe the state of the world where an old order, Pax Americana, was dying out and a new order is replacing it. I want to describe what the rupture is and how it explains the world that we are living in today. Basically I want to go through some of the major events of the past week and try to use a model or a framework to explain why things are happening the way they are.

## Global crises

Let’s go over some major crises that the world is facing as of right now. Number one, of course, is the war in Iran. Even today, we don't know why this war started. And we have absolutely no idea what the goals of the Americans are and how this war could possibly end. We do know that this war is causing massive disruption to the global economy. Also, what is very worrying is how this war is escalating. Right now the war has extended to Yemen and now the Houthis are at war with Saudi Arabia and its allies including the UAE, Pakistan, and Turkey.

This war is expanding regionally and at some point it could even link up with the war in Ukraine to create a global war. Right? So initially this war was between the United States and Iran. Remember the United States wanted to prevent Iran from getting a nuclear weapon. And now this war has extended regionally in a way that could cut off Middle East energy from the rest of the world. And this would not only lead to higher diesel prices, which is already happening, but could also lead to a global famine. It is a catastrophe, and we don't even know why this is happening.

This is the first major crisis. Second major crisis is how the world is turning right.

We've gone from left to right and the example of course is Brazil. So, earlier this week there was a presidential election in Brazil and Lula was the incumbent and he's been in politics for decades. And he's helped relieve poverty in Brazil. He brought millions out of poverty in Brazil. He's very popular. And then his opponent Flávio Bolsonaro is the son of Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest and the Bolsonaro family is known for being extremely corrupt.

There are rumors that Flávio Bolsonaro is depraved. He has a lot of sexual problems. And what is also known is that he's also very corrupt. He's engaged in bank fraud and other stuff. The poll suggested that Lula would win easily against Flávio Bolsonaro, but when it actually happened, it seemed as though Flávio Bolsonaro could have won in the first round. He could have almost gotten over 50% in the first round. He didn't, so he's going to a second round. But everyone expects him to win. And so, this is surprising for a lot of people. But not only that, but throughout Latin America, you're seeing a lot of countries shift rightwards.

Meaning that they have become very pro-Trump and pro-Israel and very nationalistic. So why is this happening? That's the second problem. The third crisis is the US–Canada trade war. We are in Toronto and so this is something that impacts us directly. We don't even know why this war started, right? But Mark Carney believes that this is a war for Canada’s sovereignty. Basically, the United States wants to control who Canada can trade with and so this initiated the trade war. But this is expanding, right? This week there were the elections in Quebec. I just came back from Quebec and the Parti Québécois won a minority government and they promised a third referendum of independence. Before the election, The Globe and Mail , Canada's national newspaper, reported that Republican operatives were in Quebec and Alberta helping secessionists plan out their electoral strategy.

So it seems that this trade war is expanding and there are different points of attack, right? So Trump wants Quebec and Alberta to secede from Canada. We know the geography of Canada. So if any one of these two provinces secedes, Canada is done for, right? You just basically split Canada in half. Mark Carney is imposing tariffs strategically against the Americans in key battleground states for the midterms because he wants to inflict pain on voters so that they vote Democrat during the midterms. This is not just a trade war. It's also a political war. And so why is this happening? That's another question that we have. And then of course there are the Gen Z protests.

And they're happening throughout the world. Earlier this year, there were the protests in Nepal. Now we're seeing major protests in India where millions of young people are out in the streets in India demanding the resignation of the election commissioner. Then in France, you have lots of young people who are not going to school and instead protesting in the streets. And you probably have seen footage from France. It is pretty violent. And the problem is there doesn't seem to be an offramp for these protests. It's almost like the French Revolution over again. In fact, they're using a lot of slogans from the previous revolutions of the past. They're talking about rebuilding the Paris Commune. This is another major issue that is happening. So, there are lots and lots of these issues and today I want to present to you a grand unified theory as to why these things are happening. My argument to you is that they are all linked together.

## How the world is constructed

To appreciate what's happening, we need to figure out how the world is constructed. And in school, what you're usually taught is that everything flows from the people, right? We live in a democracy. And so what happens is that people have norms and values. And then these norms and values become translated into law. In Canada, we call this common law, right? Common law. And this common law becomes the basis of our government, which then builds our society, which includes schools, the media, the popular culture. Then we have a military to defend our rights and our freedoms.

And this is traditionally how we understand democracies to function, right? Everything comes from an expression of the values and norms of the community. This is often called social contract theory. This comes from, of course, Jean-Jacques Rousseau who said that a society is people of their own free will coming together to surrender their freedom in return for rights from the government. The freedom to life, liberty, happiness. This is what you're taught in school and this is a theory that is most commonly accepted.

What I want to show you tonight is that this is wrong and this is the opposite of what really happens in reality. I don't have enough time to show you from first principles how this works, but I want to present you a model of the world and then apply it to current events to see if we can better explain why things are happening the way they are. Again, this is what you're traditionally taught. This is all wrong. In fact, the truth is it's the opposite. It's the opposite system.

## Plato’s allegory of the cave

To understand this, I want you to understand Plato's allegory of the cave . And Plato's allegory of the cave is a metaphor for how all of reality is constructed. The metaphor is this. Imagine a million people all lined up in a cave, a dark cave. There's no lighting. They are all seated and chained to the floor and their necks are shackled so that they can only stare forward and they're looking at a blank wall. Again this is just a thought experiment.

It's a metaphor and this is how they grew up. This is the only thing that they've known. They can only stare at the blank wall. Behind them is a great fire. A great fire. And then surrounding this great fire are people. We don't know who they are. They're called they. In the Republic written by Plato, they're just called “they.” Honestly, it doesn't really matter who they are, but they are different from us in that they're free to roam around.

And what they want to do is control us by projecting a reality on the wall so that we focus on this reality and obey whatever they tell us to be true. What they do is they take puppets and project these puppets, the shadows, onto the wall. And so now people are looking at the wall and they're seeing a movie. Now these are just shadows. These are just puppets. But this is the only thing they’ve known. What they instinctively try to do is try to figure out how this reality works. What they do is they create language, right? Language to give names to the shadows and then from these names you can create myths or stories of who these shadows are and how they got there.

And what then they do is they specialize amongst themselves to figure out what they should all do in order to better understand this reality. So some become poets or writers who create the language for this reality. Some become priests who take this reality and create a religion to explain this reality. Some become teachers who teach this reality to young people. And after a while, and again, no one knows how they got there. No one knows how these shadows got there. But after a while, they come to believe that this reality, which is all just a matrix or simulation, is the only reality that exists. And they're so convinced it's the only reality, they will kill anyone who says, "Guys, it's just a shadow on the wall. It's all fake." I want to take this metaphor, this allegory, and apply it to our reality and explain how the reality that we live in actually works.

## Layers of power

Now what I'm going to do is apply this and show how our reality is essentially just a simulation. ### Is the earth hell?

Audience question:

Professor Jiang:

That's a really good question. So, if you look at most religions, they do believe earth is hell. They believe that we're here to learn some spiritual truths and then we go. We do our penance. It’s meant to basically armor our spirituality. And we're only here for a short life, so it's not too bad. There's one religion that believes something very different, and it's called Judaism. And what makes Judaism very distinct is that it's a very temporal religion. So if you’re a Christian, if you're a Catholic, if you're a Hindu, if you're a Buddhist, if you're a Muslim, you're taught that this world doesn't really matter. You shouldn't get too involved in this world because this world is hell. This world is of Satan. And you can never defeat Satan in this world. But just avoid sin.

Practice your religion and then you will be granted access to heaven upon your death. That's what most religions teach. Judaism is a temporal religion meaning that the point of this world is to redeem it to make it ready for God's arrival. It's very different. But the idea is that God is infinite. God seeks to be everywhere. But God also seeks to know itself. And the only way to know itself is through experimentation, through error.

So God created this world and created us in order to make this world ready for God. And how do we do that? By redeeming this world and cleansing it of sin. And how do you do that? Through love, through education, through social justice. The Jews are the chosen people because they are the divine representatives of God and they're here to educate all of us in order to redeem the world. Redemption basically is to humble yourself before God and to always obey God and to love God so that God can love you unconditionally. The Jews don't believe the world is hell.
